key_insight: A fine-tuned FLAN-T5-Large model was the most accurate at detecting social isolation and social support cues in unstructured clinical notes.
clinical_relevance: Better identification of social isolation in EHR text could help healthcare teams recognize patients who may need earlier social and supportive interventions.
method: Annotated social-context spans from 326,847 adults age 50+ in clinical notes (2020–2023).
Fine-tuned FLAN-T5-Large, BERT, RoBERTa, and Gemma-2-2B for classification.
Evaluated models using accuracy, precision, recall, and macro-F1 with structured prompting to reduce overgeneralization.
evidence_signal: FLAN-T5-Large led with macro-F1 0.92±0.04, outperforming Gemma-2-2B (0.89±0.10), RoBERTa (0.80±0.21), and BERT (0.77±0.17).
watch_item: Performance was measured on annotated notes, so real-world deployment still needs external validation, workflow testing, and careful handling of ambiguous or negated context.
paper_title: Fine-Tuned Large Language Models for Detecting Social Isolation from Unstructured Clinical Notes
